# PullToRefresh

Header: `winui/ui/scrolling/PullToRefresh.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/scrolling/PullToRefresh.hpp`.

A container that refreshes its content when it is pulled past its start, with a progress indicator. The pull is a mouse drag.

A pull starts once a drag mostly along [`pull_direction()`](#pull_direction) passes 8 DIPs, and only while the content is scrolled to the edge the pull comes from. The content is anything with [`Element::scroll_info()`](../tree/element.md#scroll_info), such as a [`Scroll`](scroll.md#uiscroll) or a [`ListView`](../controls/list-view.md#uilistview). It follows the pointer, and a 100 DIP visualizer slides in behind it, its indicator turning with the pull. The indicator is a Refresh symbol, or what [`set_visualizer_content()`](#set_visualizer_content) installs. Releasing past 80 % of the visualizer (Pending) refreshes: the state goes to Refreshing, [`on_refresh_requested()`](#on_refresh_requested) fires once, and the refresh lasts until the app calls [`complete_refresh()`](#complete_refresh). [`ui::PullToRefresh`](#uipulltorefresh) is the declarative form.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Control<ui::PullToRefresh> refresh;
window.set_content(ui::PullToRefresh{
    .height               = 400.0f,
    .on_refresh_requested = [&refresh] {
        // Start reloading; when the new data is in (now or later, e.g. from a timer):
        refresh->complete_refresh(); // back to Idle
    },
    .control              = refresh,
    .content              = ui::Scroll{.content = ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
        ui::Text{.text = "Item 1"},
        ui::Text{.text = "Item 2"},
    }}},
});

// Imperatively, pulling up from the bottom:
auto ptr = std::make_unique<ui::PullToRefreshControl>();
ui::ScrollControl* scroll = ptr->set_content(std::make_unique<ui::ScrollControl>());
ptr->set_pull_direction(ui::RefreshPullDirection::BottomToTop);
ptr->on_refresh_state_changed([](const ui::PullToRefreshStateChangedArgs& args) { /* e.g. show a status text */ });
ptr->request_refresh(); // refresh programmatically, without a pull
```

## `ui::PullToRefresh`

Pull one child with the mouse to refresh it. Builds a [ui::PullToRefreshControl](#uipulltorefreshcontrol). on_refresh_requested fires once, and the app calls [`.control`](#uipulltorefresh-control)'s complete_refresh() when the work it started, typically an async data fetch, has finished.

Example: 
```cpp
void start_fetch(ui::Action done); // the app's own async work
ui::Control<ui::PullToRefresh> pull;

window.set_content(ui::PullToRefresh{
    .height               = 400.0f,
    .on_refresh_requested = [&]
    {
        start_fetch([&] { pull->complete_refresh(); });
    },
    .control = pull,
    .content = ui::Scroll{.content = ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
        ui::Text{.text = "Item 1"},
        ui::Text{.text = "Item 2"},
    }}},
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::PullToRefresh{
    .pull_direction, .visualizer_orientation, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width,
    .min_height, .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible,
    .tool_tip, .accessibility, .on_refresh_requested, .on_refresh_state_changed,
    .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down,
    .on_wheel, .control, .content, .visualizer_content
}
```

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| <span id="uipulltorefresh-visualizer_orientation"></span>`visualizer_orientation` | `ui::Binding<ui::RefreshVisualizerOrientation>` | `{ui::RefreshVisualizerOrientation::Auto}` | How the indicator is turned. Auto turns it along the pull. |
| <span id="uipulltorefresh-on_refresh_requested"></span>`on_refresh_requested` | `ui::Callback<void()>` |  | Fires once per refresh; call complete_refresh() on [`.control`](#uipulltorefresh-control) when done. |
| <span id="uipulltorefresh-on_refresh_state_changed"></span>`on_refresh_state_changed` | `ui::Callback<void(const ui::PullToRefreshStateChangedArgs&)>` |  | Fires with the old and the new state (Idle, Interacting, Pending, Refreshing). |
| <span id="uipulltorefresh-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uipulltorefresh-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uipulltorefresh-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uipulltorefresh-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |

| <span id="uipulltorefresh-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uipulltorefresh-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::PullToRefresh>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |
| <span id="uipulltorefresh-content"></span>`content` | `ui::Spec` |  | The pulled content, typically a [ui::Scroll](scroll.md#uiscroll) or a list. |


### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Implement these instead of [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) and [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete [Element](../tree/element.md) must size itself); [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) set, which the base already did.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Position children within the rect [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange) settled on (also in [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds), window DIPs). Default: nothing, for a leaf.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

What the control draws, in layout coordinates; [render()](../tree/element.md#render) has already applied the visual layer. A container draws its children through their [render()](../tree/element.md#render), never their [render_override()](#render_override).

### pointer_override

```cpp
bool pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

Drives the pull from a mouse drag; other pointer input goes to the content.

### handled_pointer_override

```cpp
void handled_pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

A press and release the content took still start and end a pull.

### clear_dirty_override

```cpp
void clear_dirty_override(DirtyFlags flags) override
```

Clears the dirty flags of the content and of the indicator, whether it shows or not.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

Advances the settle, Pending pulse and Refreshing spin animations, and ticks the content and the indicator.

## struct PullToRefreshStateChangedArgs

What `on_refresh_state_changed` gets: the state before and after the change.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `old_state` | `PullToRefreshState` | `PullToRefreshState::Idle` | The state it left. |
| `new_state` | `PullToRefreshState` | `PullToRefreshState::Idle` | The state it is in now. |

## Enumerations

### RefreshPullDirection

```cpp
enum class RefreshPullDirection
```

Which way the content is pulled.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `LeftToRight` | Pulled rightwards from the left edge, while scrolled to the start. |
| `TopToBottom` | Pulled down from the top, while scrolled to the start (the default). |
| `RightToLeft` | Pulled leftwards from the right edge, while scrolled to the end. |
| `BottomToTop` | Pulled up from the bottom, while scrolled to the end. |

### RefreshVisualizerOrientation

```cpp
enum class RefreshVisualizerOrientation
```

How the indicator is turned.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Auto` | Turned along the pull. |
| `Normal` | Upright. |
| `Rotate90DegreesCounterclockwise` | Turned by +90 degrees. |
| `Rotate270DegreesCounterclockwise` | Turned by -90 degrees. |

### PullToRefreshState

```cpp
enum class PullToRefreshState
```

Where a pull to refresh is: idle, being pulled, armed or refreshing.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Idle` | Not pulled and not refreshing. |
| `Interacting` | Pulled, but not far enough to refresh. |
| `Pending` | Pulled far enough, so a release now refreshes. |
| `Refreshing` | Refreshing until complete_refresh(). |
